entry: Seven-a-side ball sport played mainly by women and girls. It is one of a few sports created exclusively for them and is most popular in the [[Commonwealth of Nations]]. Originating in [[England]] in 1895 as a modified form of [[Basketball|basketball]], it was standardized internationally in 1960. The objective is to shoot through the defender's goal ring while stopping the opposition from shooting through their own. Players are restricted to zones of the court by their positions and may hold the ball for only three seconds. More than 20 million people play the sport in more than 80 countries, according to World Netball. The World Netball Championships and Commonwealth Games are held every four years. In 1995 the sport's governing body became an International Olympic Committee recognized federation, but netball has not yet been played at the Olympics.

American subscription [[Streaming media|streaming]] service for films and television shows. Founded in 1997 by Marc Randolph and Reed Hastings as a [[DVD]] rental service, it began streaming in 2007. It distributes original and acquired content in multiple languages. Netflix is the most-subscribed global streaming media service, with more than 325 million paid memberships in more than 190 countries. By 2022, Netflix Original productions made up half of its library in the [[United States]]. The company has also published mobile video games.

Country in northwestern Europe and the Caribbean. The Netherlands, also informally known as [[Holland]], is the largest of the four constituent countries of the Kingdom of the Netherlands. European Netherlands borders [[Germany]] to the east and [[Belgium]] to the south, with a coastline on the North Sea. About 26% of the country lies below sea level, largely on [[Polder|polders]] created by land reclamation that began in the 14th century. During the [[Dutch Golden Age]], its trading companies established colonies and trading posts. The country was invaded and occupied by Nazi Germany in 1940, and the occupation lasted until the end of the war in 1945. A parliamentary constitutional monarchy since 1848, it is a founding member of the [[European Union]]. [[Amsterdam]] is the nominal capital, while [[The Hague]] houses the main national political institutions. It was the first country to legalize same-sex marriage, in 2001.

Computational model used in [[Machine learning|machine learning]], loosely inspired by biological neural networks. It consists of connected units called artificial [[Neuron|neurons]], which pass real-number signals along weighted connections. Networks with at least two hidden layers are typically called deep neural networks. Training is compute-intensive and is often accelerated by [[Graphics processing unit|graphics processing units]] (GPUs). Convolutional neural networks improved computer vision, while transformer architectures, which introduced attention mechanisms, have been the basis of [[Large language model|large language models]]. Neural networks are used for chatbots, text, image and video generation, and robotics.

Branch of medicine concerned with diagnosing and treating disorders of the nervous system, which comprises the brain, spinal cord and peripheral nerves. Neurologists treat conditions including [[Stroke|stroke]], [[Epilepsy|epilepsy]], [[Parkinson's disease]], [[Multiple sclerosis]], [[Migraine|migraine]] and dementias such as Alzheimer's disease. Neurology is a nonsurgical specialty; its surgical counterpart is neurosurgery. Clinical practice relies heavily on [[Neuroscience|neuroscience]], the scientific study of the nervous system. In the United States and Canada, neurologists typically complete residency training after medical school, and total training takes eight to ten years. Neurologists may also take part in clinical research and trials. The academic discipline began between the 17th and 18th centuries.

1984 science fiction novel by William Gibson. Set in the near future, it follows Case, a [[Hacker|hacker]] recruited by a powerful [[Artificial intelligence|artificial intelligence]] for a heist. It was Gibson's debut and the first book of the Sprawl trilogy. The novel popularized the concept of cyberspace and defined major conventions of [[Cyberpunk|cyberpunk]]. Critics differ on whether it ignited the genre or was carried by it. It became an underground hit and is the first and only novel to win the Hugo Award, the Nebula Award for Best Novel and the Philip K. Dick Award. In 2005 *Time* named it one of its All-Time 100 Novels.

Electrically excitable nerve cell, the primary cell of the [[Nervous system|nervous system]]. Neurons are the main components of nervous tissue in all animals except sponges and placozoans. Most receive signals through dendrites and the cell body, then send signals down a long axon, usually releasing [[Neurotransmitter|neurotransmitters]] at synapses. When voltage changes enough, the neuron generates an all-or-nothing electrochemical pulse called an action potential. Neurons are typically classified by function as sensory, motor or interneurons. Most are generated during brain development and childhood, and neurogenesis largely ceases in adulthood in most brain areas. The ability to generate electric signals first appeared some 700 to 800 million years ago.

Scientific study of the nervous system, its functions and its disorders. The field is multidisciplinary, combining physiology, anatomy, molecular biology, [[Psychology|psychology]], physics, [[Computer science|computer science]], chemistry, [[Medicine|medicine]] and statistics to study [[Neuron|neurons]], glia and neural circuits. Eric Kandel called the biological basis of learning, memory, behavior, perception and consciousness the "epic challenge" of the biological sciences. The study of the nervous system dates to ancient Egypt, and [[Hippocrates]] argued that the brain was the seat of intelligence. [[Galen]] later observed that brain damage impaired mental faculties. [[Luigi Galvani]]'s work in the late 1700s set the stage for studying electrical excitability. Camillo Golgi's staining method, developed in the late 1890s, was used by [[Santiago Ramón y Cajal]] to reveal individual neurons.

Signaling molecule released by a [[Neuron|neuron]] to affect another cell across a synapse. The target cell may be another neuron, a gland or a muscle cell. Neurotransmitters are usually stored in synaptic vesicles and released into the synaptic cleft, where they bind to receptors. The receptor determines whether the effect is excitation, inhibition or modulation. Many are synthesized from simple precursors such as [[Amino acid|amino acids]], and monoamines such as [[Dopamine|dopamine]] and [[Serotonin|serotonin]] are formed by altering a single amino acid. Metabolic gases such as [[Nitric oxide|nitric oxide]] and [[Carbon monoxide|carbon monoxide]] also act like neurotransmitters. More than 100 have been identified, and common ones include glutamate, GABA, acetylcholine, glycine and norepinephrine. They are therapeutic targets for disorders such as [[Parkinson's disease]] and [[Depression (mood)|depression]].

19th-century historicist palace on a rugged hill in the foothills of the [[Alps]], near the Austrian border in [[Bavaria]], Germany. King Ludwig II commissioned it as a retreat and in honor of composer [[Richard Wagner]]. Built from 1869 to 1892 in the Neo-Romanesque style, it drew on the design of medieval knights' castles. Ludwig financed it largely with his own fortune and borrowing, and he died in 1886. The castle opened to the public shortly afterward and attracts more than 1.3 million visitors a year. It has been part of the [[World Heritage Site|UNESCO World Heritage Site]] since 2025.

Electrically neutral elementary particle with an extremely small mass. It interacts with other matter only through the [[Weak interaction|weak interaction]] and gravity, so it usually passes through matter undetected. Neutrinos are created in weak decays such as [[Beta decay|beta decay]], and most of those detected on Earth come from nuclear reactions inside the [[Sun]]. [[Wolfgang Pauli]] postulated the particle in 1930 to explain how beta decay conserved energy, momentum and angular momentum. Neutrinos come in three flavors (electron, muon and tau) and oscillate between them in flight, which shows that they have mass. Their individual masses are not yet known, but their sum is less than 0.120 eV/c².

Collapsed core of a massive star, left after a supernova. Neutron stars are the second-smallest and second-densest known class of stellar objects, surpassed only by [[Black hole|black holes]]. They have a radius on the order of 10 km (6 miles) and a mass of about 1.4 [[Solar mass|solar masses]]. Estimates put the number in the [[Milky Way]] at around one billion, and at a minimum several hundred million, although many have cooled considerably. Most detected neutron stars are [[Pulsar|pulsars]] or part of a binary system. In 2017 the LIGO and Virgo observatories detected [[Gravitational wave|gravitational waves]] from the merger of two neutron stars, GW170817, the first direct detection of such waves from that kind of event. The merger is associated with kilonovae and short [[Gamma-ray burst|gamma-ray bursts]].

River in northwestern Russia, flowing from [[Lake Ladoga]] to the Gulf of Finland. Despite a length of 74 km (46 mi), it is the fourth-largest river in Europe by average discharge, after the [[Volga]], [[Danube]] and [[Rhine]]. It is the only river flowing from Lake Ladoga and flows through [[Saint Petersburg]]. The river is navigable throughout and forms part of the Volga–Baltic Waterway and White Sea–Baltic Canal. Historical events include the Battle of the Neva in 1240, which gave [[Alexander Nevsky]] his name, the founding of Saint Petersburg in 1703, and the [[Siege of Leningrad]] during [[World War II]]. A catastrophic flood in 1824 inundated much of the city.

Landlocked state in the Western United States, bordering Oregon, Idaho, Utah, Arizona and California. Its capital is Carson City, and [[Las Vegas]] is the largest city. Statehood came on October 31, 1864, during the Civil War, after a population boom that followed the discovery of [[Silver|silver]] at the Comstock Lode in 1859. Tourism, built partly on legalized [[Gambling|gambling]], remains the largest employer. Nevada is the driest U.S. state, and most of it is [[Desert|desert]] or semi-arid. The federal government manages 80.1% of its land. Nevada is the only U.S. state where prostitution is legal, though not in its most populous counties.

2005 science fiction novel by British author [[Kazuo Ishiguro]]. It is Ishiguro's sixth novel, set in an alternative 1990s England, and follows students at Hailsham, an elite boarding school. They are clones raised to donate their organs, and the narrator, Kathy, reflects on her friendships with Ruth and Tommy as the students learn the truth about their futures. The novel explores friendship, memory and what it means to be human. It was shortlisted for the Man Booker Prize and named the best novel of 2005 by *Time* magazine. A film adaptation directed by Mark Romanek was released in 2010.

Second studio album by the American rock band [[Nirvana (band)|Nirvana]], released on September 24, 1991. Produced by Butch Vig, it blends [[Alternative rock|alternative rock]] and grunge with punk-inspired hard rock. Its lead single, "Smells Like Teen Spirit", reached the Top 10 of the Billboard Hot 100. The album topped the Billboard 200 in January 1992 and is generally credited with bringing grunge to a mainstream audience. Its lyrics address social alienation and frustration, and [[Kurt Cobain]] was dubbed the "voice of his generation". It has sold more than 30 million copies worldwide.

British Conservative politician; prime minister of the United Kingdom, 1937–40. Chamberlain is known for his policy of appeasement toward [[Nazi Germany]], especially the [[Munich|Munich Agreement]] of 1938, which ceded the German-speaking Sudetenland of [[Czechoslovakia]] to Germany. He declared war on Germany after its [[Invasion of Poland|invasion of Poland]] in 1939. He resigned in May 1940 when Labour and Liberal leaders would not serve under him, and [[Winston Churchill]] succeeded him. Critics, notably in *Guilty Men* (1940), blamed him for failing to prepare for war, while some later historians argue that war in 1938 would have been disastrous.

Eclectic range of spiritual and religious beliefs and practices that grew rapidly in Western society in the early 1970s. It drew on [[Western esotericism|Western esoteric]] traditions, including Spiritualism and Theosophy, and on the 1960s counterculture and the Human Potential Movement. Common beliefs include a holistic divinity that pervades the universe and the spiritual authority of the self. Practices include [[Meditation|meditation]], [[Astrology|astrology]] and channeling, and adherents often seek healing through [[Alternative medicine|alternative medicine]]. The name refers to the expected Age of Aquarius. Criticism has come from Christians as well as modern Pagan and Indigenous communities. Scholars of religious studies have researched the movement since the 1990s, and adherents increasingly rejected the term by the early 21st century.

Largest island in the Bismarck Archipelago, part of [[Papua New Guinea]] and roughly the size of [[Taiwan]]. Its main towns are Rabaul, Kokopo and Kimbe. Formed largely by volcanic processes, it has active volcanoes including Ulawun, its highest point at 2,334 m (7,657 ft). A major eruption of Tavurvur in 1994 destroyed much of Rabaul, the East New Britain provincial capital, and the capital moved to Kokopo. William Dampier became the first known British visitor in 1700 and named it Nova Britannia. As part of [[New Guinea|German New Guinea]] from 1884, the island was called Neupommern. Australian forces captured it in 1914, and it was later administered as a [[League of Nations]] mandate.

Province of eastern [[Canada]], one of the three Maritime provinces, about 83% forested. Its population of 775,610 (2021 census) is about two-thirds English-speaking and one-third French-speaking. The province is home to most of the cultural region of [[Acadia]] and most Acadians, whose variety of French is called Acadian French. British authorities deported Acadians en masse from 1755 to 1764 in the Great Upheaval. The colony was created in 1784, after many loyalists arrived following the American Revolution, and the province joined Confederation in 1867. The Official Languages Act of 1969 recognized French alongside English. Tourism accounts for 9% of the labor force.

French collectivity of islands in the southwest Pacific Ocean, about 1,210 km (750 mi) east of [[Australia]]. Its main island is Grande Terre, and it has a unique legal status set out in a dedicated chapter of the French Constitution. The population of 264,596 (April 2025 census) includes Kanak people, who make up 41%, and the capital is Nouméa. The territory forms part of [[Melanesia]]. [[James Cook]] sighted it in 1774 and named it after [[Scotland]]. Blackbirding, the kidnapping and forced labor of islanders on plantations, was practiced by French and Australian traders. [[Nickel]] mining accounts for about 90% of exports. Referendums on independence held in 2018, 2020 and 2021 rejected separation from France, though boycotts by Kanak groups lowered turnout in the last vote. The Lagoons of New Caledonia have been a [[World Heritage Site|UNESCO World Heritage Site]] since 2008.

Series of economic, social and political reforms introduced in the [[United States]] by President [[Franklin D. Roosevelt]] in response to the [[Great Depression]]. The First New Deal (1933–35) aimed at relief, recovery and reform of the financial system. Its measures included the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation, the Securities and Exchange Commission and the Civilian Conservation Corps, which employed young men on government land. The Second New Deal (1935–38) created the National Labor Relations Act, which guaranteed the right to organize [[Trade union|trade unions]], and the Social Security Act. Historians still debate its effectiveness, though most accept that full employment was not achieved until the United States entered [[World War II]] in 1941. Some econometric studies argue that its cartel-style policies prolonged the Depression.

Capital city of India, part of the National Capital Territory of [[Delhi]]. It seats the three branches of the [[Government of India]], including the Rashtrapati Bhavan presidential palace, Parliament House and the Supreme Court. British architects Edwin Lutyens and Herbert Baker designed the city. [[George V]] announced the shift of the capital from Calcutta at the 1911 Delhi Durbar and laid the foundation stone. The city was inaugurated on February 13, 1931. The municipality, administered by the New Delhi Municipal Council, mostly covers Lutyens' Delhi.

Region of six states in the northeastern United States: Connecticut, Maine, Massachusetts, New Hampshire, Rhode Island and Vermont. It borders [[New York (state)|New York]] to the west and the Canadian provinces of [[New Brunswick]] and [[Quebec]]. [[Boston]] is the largest city, and Greater Boston houses more than half of the region's population. The Pilgrims established Plymouth Colony in 1620, and Puritans later founded Massachusetts Bay Colony. Residents of Boston threw British tea into the harbor, and British punitive laws led to the first battles of the [[American Revolutionary War]] in 1775. The region was the first in the United States transformed by the [[Industrial Revolution]]. Its physical geography includes a narrow coastal plain and the northern end of the [[Appalachian Mountains]].

Professional American football team in the [[National Football League]], based in the Greater Boston area. Founded in 1959 as the Boston Patriots, the team was a charter member of the American Football League before joining the NFL in 1970. It moved to Foxborough, Massachusetts, in 1971 and plays at Gillette Stadium. Under coach [[Bill Belichick]] and quarterback [[Tom Brady]], the team dominated from 2001 to the 2019 season, and it holds the record for the most [[Super Bowl]] appearances (12). The franchise has won six Super Bowls, tied with the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]] for the most. Owner Robert Kraft bought the team in 1994.
